alignments.note: Waw rendered by the connective *therefore* the ASV writes for it (rule 14); the ASV places it postpositively, so the unit stands apart from the verb's words under rule 25.

Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), rendered as light verb plus complement *make a distinction*; head on the complement carrying the lexeme (rule 44). The *a* belongs to that nominal expression under rule 15. Unit discontinuous around *therefore*.
First `בֵּין` of the first pair takes the written *between* (rule 26).
Article on the noun takes the phrase's single written *the*; English reorders it before the adjective (rule 47).
Noun takes its own word.
Agreement article on the attributive; the phrase's one *the* went to the noun's article under rule 47.
Adjective rendered *clean*.
`בֵּין X לְ Y` → *between X and Y*: the `לְ` stands where the connective stands and takes the *and* (rule 26); no waw is present to claim it.
Assimilated article supplied by MACULA as a bracketed token; it takes the written *the* (rule 12).
Substantival adjective rendered *unclean*.
Waw takes the *and* written for it (rule 14).
This `בֵּין` opens the second pair, and the ASV writes a *between* for that pair; counting *between*s against pairs, it is not the repeated preposition inside a pair (rule 26).
Article on the noun takes the phrase's single written *the* (rule 47).
Noun rendered *fowl*.
Agreement article on the attributive; the phrase's one *the* went to the noun's article (rule 47).
Adjective rendered *unclean*.
The `לְ` of the second member takes the connective *and* (rule 26).
Assimilated article takes the written *the* (rule 12).
Substantival adjective rendered *clean*.
Waw takes the *and* written for it (rule 14).
Negative takes its own *not*; the ASV writes it as a separate word, so nothing is fused (rule 35).

Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), rendered as light verb plus adjectival complement *make ... abominable*; head on the complement under rule 44, since *make* alone names nothing. Unit discontinuous around *not* and the object (rule 25).
Object marker H853 with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Noun rendered *souls*.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *your* (rule 18).
Preposition takes the written *by* (rule 11).
Assimilated article; the ASV writes *by beast* with no article, so nothing answers to it (rules 12, 29).
Noun rendered *beast*.
Waw rendered by the connective *or* the ASV wrote for it (rule 14).
Preposition takes the written *by*.
Assimilated article with no *the* written for it (rules 12, 29).
Noun rendered *bird*.
Waw rendered *or* (rule 14).
Preposition takes the written *by*.
`כֹל` is what the ASV's *anything* renders; the quantifier word belongs to the present `כֹּל` morpheme rather than being a supplied determiner on a bare noun (rule 15).

Relative rendered by the pronominal adverb *wherewith*; the one English word carries the relation as well as the relative, and no separate preposition or resumptive morpheme stands here to divide it (rules 22, 30).
Finite verb rendered *teemeth*.
Article takes the written *the*.
Noun rendered *ground*.
Relative rendered *which*.
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).

The ASV recasts the dative `לְ` of separation as *from*; the preposition takes the word written for its own relation (rule 11). The competing reading marks it `unrepresented` on the ground that *from* reverses the Hebrew relation, but nothing else in the clause answers for the word.
Suffix rendered by the object pronoun *you* (rule 18).
`לְ` + infinitive construct recast as a role phrase; the preposition takes the written function word *as* (rule 52's reading that a written word, not only a complementizer, is the preposition's).
Infinitive construct rendered by the predicate adjective *unclean*, which carries its lexeme.

review_notes: Two `בֵּין` pairs, each opened by a written *between* (rule 26); the `לְ` of each second member takes the *and*, and both waws keep the connectives written for them.
Both light-verb renderings (*make a distinction*, *make ... abominable*) head on their complements under rule 44 rather than on *make*.
All four bracketed assimilated articles read individually: the two in the `בֵּין` phrases take written *the*s, the two before *beast* and *bird* are unrepresented.
